item.title: Engineered Medical Gloves Cut Bacterial Transmission by Up to 99%
item.dc:creator: Julianna LeMieux, PhD
item.description:
Researchers developed innovative medical gloves with microscopic fluid-repelling surfaces that reduce bacterial attachment and transmission by up to 99%, potentially helping prevent hospital-acquired infections.

The post Engineered Medical Gloves Cut Bacterial Transmission by Up to 99% appeared first on GEN - Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology News.

item.title: CGT Manufacturing Success in Asia Requires Standardization and Flexibility
item.dc:creator: Corinna Singleman, PhD
item.description:
Asia's CGT therapy pipeline is expanding rapidly, but the region's fragmented regulatory, manufacturing, and supply-chain landscape creates a distinctive challenge: how to build processes that are standardized enough to be reproducible.

The post CGT Manufacturing Success in Asia Requires Standardization and Flexibility appeared first on GEN - Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology News.

item.title: Coronary Artery Disease Genetics Map Links Risk Variants to Genes and Cell Types
item.dc:creator: Sophia Ktori
item.description:
Researchers create a multiomic map of human coronary artery disease that links disease-associated genetic variants with candidate disease-relevant cell types and target genes.

The post Coronary Artery Disease Genetics Map Links Risk Variants to Genes and Cell Types appeared first on GEN - Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology News.

item.title: Why Genomics Won’t Converge on One Technology
item.dc:creator: Corinna Singleman, PhD
item.description:
In this guest commentary Barrett Bready, MD, CEO of Nabsys provides insight on understanding why and when genomics relies on short-read and long-read sequencing and why keeping both are essential.

The post Why Genomics Won’t Converge on One Technology appeared first on GEN - Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology News.

item.title: Alzheimer’s Study Shows Gal3 Shapes Aβ Remodeling and Microglial Responses
item.dc:creator: Sophia Ktori
item.description:
Researchers identified a role for the protein galectin-3 in Alzheimer's disease, with the result of brain tissue analyses and experiments in mice indicating that galectin-3 acts as a modulator of Aβ remodeling, lysosomal homeostasis, and microglial responses.

The post Alzheimer’s Study Shows Gal3 Shapes Aβ Remodeling and Microglial Responses appeared first on GEN - Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology News.
